method: Both the retiring SwissJob scraper and the new Core adapter were replayed offline against this SAME sealed capture, so the parity below is byte-level.

transport_contract.payload: props.pageProps.initialData inside __NEXT_DATA__ (identical to the tRPC query cache on page 1, verified)

portal_ceiling.cause: ?page=N is ignored server-side: page 2 renders page 1's data (currentPage: 1). The client fetches later pages through a route that is not exposed in the rendered payload.
portal_ceiling.producer_behaviour: The scraper paginated against the same ignored parameter and lost the eight offers in silence; its PAGE_SIZE=1 comment ('server enforces limit=1') is stale — the portal serves twenty per page.
portal_ceiling.core_behaviour: Asks for page 2 ONCE so that real pagination would be followed if the portal ever honours it; otherwise stops, logs the shortfall and publishes announced/harvested/shortfall in the cursor. The run stays COMPLETE: a permanent portal limitation must not freeze last_complete_at and turn the staleness alert into noise.

deliberate_improvements.what: identity is the portal's own numeric job id
deliberate_improvements.evidence: every row carries `id` and the canonical URL ends with it (20 of 20)
deliberate_improvements.effect: a retitled offer keeps one identity; the scraper hashed title|company|url

deliberate_improvements.what: the shortfall is counted and logged
deliberate_improvements.effect: a 29 % blind spot becomes visible instead of silent

deliberate_improvements.evidence: the scraper paged until an empty page; the payload itself declares totalPages
deliberate_improvements.effect: less traffic for the same data
